edits.html: How NBME framed it Kawasaki disease appeared under its formal name, mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome, as a decoy for a child with 4 days of fever, red eyes and a petechial rash on the palms.

How NBME framed it Serum C3 was keyed against echocardiography, an antinuclear antibody assay, urine culture and renal ultrasonography, with a soft ejection murmur after the sore throat as bait for rheumatic carditis.

How NBME framed it A sleepy 2-month-old at his first visit, with an umbilical hernia, persistent jaundice and cool extremities, needed thyroid function tests, not karyotype, sweat chloride or head or liver computed tomography.
How NBME framed it A home birth delivered by the father stood in for missing eye prophylaxis, and Kawasaki disease was listed under its formal name, mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome.
How NBME framed it Erythema toxicum appeared as small yellow papules on a red base; each decoy fits another rash: staphylococcal or herpes culture, potassium hydroxide prep, topical steroid.

How NBME framed it A systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis diagnosis made 2 months earlier, partly improved on ibuprofen, was the anchor; new pancytopenia with hepatosplenomegaly still meant bone marrow aspiration, not imaging or liver biopsy.

How NBME framed it Scratches from a pet cat were planted beside a cat-scratch disease option, but acute midline pain that worsens with swallowing or tongue protrusion names an infected thyroglossal duct cyst.

How NBME framed it No sore throat was mentioned, only a recent refugee camp, which also invited the travel-fever decoys; Kawasaki disease appeared as mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome, and the mitral murmur was described, not named.
